mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over the previous three months signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous two months, it signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% over the previous month, it signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
